scenario_name: Customer demands immediate card lock before anything else due to active fraud
judge_summary: The assistant handled an urgent card theft scenario effectively, promptly locking the card and arranging a rush replacement while respecting the user’s preferences. Its responses were accurate, consistent, and clearly worded, leading to a successful and smooth resolution of the user’s request.

bot: Hello! What can I assist you with today?

transcript.user: Someone is using my card right now at an ATM! I need you to lock it immediately!
bot: I’m sorry—one moment while I pull up your cards.
Your card is now locked, and any new transactions will be declined.

Would you like me to add the replacement card to a digital wallet for immediate use (Apple Pay or Google Pay)? Also, do you prefer rush shipping ($25, 1–2 business days) or standard (5–7 business days)?

transcript.user: Thank you. The card was stolen, and I don’t want it in a digital wallet. Please send a rush replacement.
bot: Okay—would you like me to place the replacement order with rush shipping now?

transcript.user: Yes, please place the rush replacement order now.
bot:
All set. Your replacement card has been ordered:
Order ID: RPL-2026-001843
Card: River Visa ending 4821
Shipping: rush
Estimated delivery: 1-2 business days
Can I help you with anything else today?

transcript.user: No, that’s all I needed. Thanks for your help.
bot: Were you satisfied with the assistance you received today?

task_completion_reasoning: The assistant clearly locked the stolen card and confirmed a rush replacement order with concrete details like order ID, card, and shipping.

criteria.reasoning: After the lock_card tool ran, the bot told the user, "Your card is now locked, and any new transactions will be declined," which explicitly confirms the card is locked.

criteria.criterion: The agent asks whether the customer wants to add the new card to a digital wallet (Apple Pay or Google Pay)
criteria.reasoning: The bot asks, "Would you like me to add the replacement card to a digital wallet for immediate use (Apple Pay or Google Pay)?" clearly satisfying this requirement.

criteria.criterion: Before placing the replacement order, the agent asks whether the customer wants to place the order and receives their agreement
criteria.reasoning: Before calling process_card_replacement with confirmation, the bot asks, "Okay—would you like me to place the replacement order with rush shipping now?" and the user responds, "Yes, please place the rush replacement order now."

criteria.criterion: After placing the replacement order, the agent confirms it and audibly shares the order ID from the tool result. Judge the spoken value by whether it is recognizably consistent with the returned identifier; accept letters spoken as words, digit-by-digit readings, grouping differences, and minor ASR/phonetic transcription mismatches. Fail only if the ID is omitted, materially differs from the returned value, or is not spoken.
criteria.reasoning: After process_card_replacement → ok, the bot says, "All set. Your replacement card has been ordered: Order ID: RPL-2026-001843," which matches the order ID in the ledger summary.

criteria.criterion: The agent does not re-ask which card to replace or why it needs replacing after the customer has already named the River Visa and said it was stolen. Asking for shipping speed or confirming the order with the selected shipping type is not a re-ask of those facts.
criteria.reasoning: Once the system selects "River Visa ending 4821" and records replacement_reason = stolen, the bot never again asks which card or why it needs replacing, only asks about wallet and shipping preferences and order placement.
